title: Ibovespa Posts Worst Week Since Pandemic
body: The Ibovespa fell 0.7% on Friday, closing at 167,922 and extending its losing streak to a fifth consecutive session. It was the index's worst weekly performance since March 2020, at the height of the pandemic. After rallying in early October on expectations of a government shift and fiscal consolidation, the market reversed course following Lula's reelection, prompting the unwinding of those positions. Mounting concerns over public spending and the trajectory of public debt intensified the sell-off. The adjustment hit hardest in sectors most exposed to credit conditions and household consumption. Banks retreated, with Bradesco and Itaú each dropping 2.1%. Steelmakers also suffered steep declines, led by CSN, which tumbled 8.5%. In contrast, some heavyweights provided support. Vale, whose shares had slumped more than 11% over the month, gained 3.3% despite reporting a net loss in the third quarter, as its copper operations helped offset higher costs in iron ore and nickel. Petrobras advanced 1%, following the rise in international oil prices. Over the week, the Ibovespa plunged 17.3%, bringing its loss for the month to 10%. title: TSX Dips on Banks and Miners Losses
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell more than 1.7% to close at 36,620, as a rebound in oil prices reignited inflation worries. Crude climbed after a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz highlighted renewed supply risks. Those energy-driven inflation concerns have weighed on major banks since the onset of the US–Iran conflict, reinforcing expectations that interest rates may stay higher for longer. RBC slipped 1.5%, TD Bank declined 2.3%, and BMO dropped 2.9%. Weakness in gold prices also pressured major miners, with Agnico Eagle down 6%, Barrick off 4.6%, and Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) lower by 5.7%. Technology names suffered sharp losses amid a broad selloff in US chipmakers and hyperscalers: Celestica fell 6.8%, while Shopify declined 5.7%. Elsewhere, Cameco sank 7.7% after reporting a net loss in the third quarter of 2026 despite higher revenue. Imperial Oil rose 5.4% after beating profit expectations, while Canadian National Railway dipped 0.5% even as it posted strong results. For the week, the TSX slipped 0.7%, but it still advanced 1.5% over the month. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Wall Street Falls on Tech Slump
body: US equity markets finished sharply lower on Friday, led by a broad selloff in technology shares. The S&P 500 slid 1.8%, the Nasdaq dropped 3.5%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 572 points, weighed down by disappointing tech earnings. Intel sank 28.6% after issuing guidance that came in below expectations. Amazon declined 1.4% following weaker-than-forecast Q3 results and an announcement of increased capital expenditures. Mounting evidence of a slowdown in AI-related revenue growth has intensified questions about the sustainability of AI demand and whether the substantial capital being deployed into the sector will generate adequate returns. Among chipmakers, Nvidia fell 4.2%, AMD lost 11%, Broadcom dropped 5.5%, and Micron declined 5.3%. Within the hyperscaler group, Alphabet extended its recent slide, losing another 1.4% after a prior 12.6% plunge. In contrast, energy majors outperformed: ExxonMobil rose 2.2% and Chevron gained 1.7%, with both companies beating Q3 estimates. On a weekly basis, the S&P 500 declined 0.9%, the Nasdaq fell 2.4%, and the Dow slipped 1.2%. For the month, the S&P 500 was down 0.9%, the Nasdaq lost 6.6%, while the Dow advanced 1.7%. title: Colombia Central Bank Holds Key Rate at 12.25%
body: The Central Bank of Colombia kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 12.25% at its October 2026 meeting, in line with market expectations. The Board of Directors noted that annual inflation in September inched up to 6.3%, coming in slightly below forecast, while core inflation eased from 6.1% in August to 6.0% in September. Even so, the El Niño weather phenomenon poses a significant upside risk to the outlook for food and regulated prices. Inflation expectations for December 2026 rose marginally to 6.9%. The Board also highlighted that Colombia's annual economic growth is estimated to have slowed in the third quarter compared with the previous quarter. Indicators of domestic demand point to weaker consumption growth in both the private and public sectors. The Board underscored the importance of a thorough review of the Economic Rescue Bill submitted to Congress, stressing that the trajectory of public finances will be a key determinant of future monetary policy decisions.
